ledger.claim: The driver ended this pickup in silence, and the platform's own records show it. The rider's message at 11:02:47 - "coming down now", delivered 11:02:48 and read by the driver at 11:03:17 - is a coordinating message about the rider's own position sent inside the waiting window, which is what limb (a) of POL-NS-04 requires. The driver had asked "where are you" at 11:00:52 (read by the rider 11:01:32), and the rider answered 75 seconds after reading it. The driver's only message in the whole log is that 11:00:52 one: he posted no reply within 120 seconds of the rider's message, and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so limb (b) holds as well - the driver neither typed nor called before cancelling at 11:07:18, 271 seconds after the rider's message and 241 seconds after reading it. A driver who has been told the rider is on the way down and who then cancels without a word has not been left waiting by the rider's failure to communicate; the failure to communicate is his.

Two admissible artifacts contradict each other directly on rider presence, no clause resolves the conflict, and limb (b) of POL-NS-09 therefore sends this case to a human reviewer. EV-CHAT-03303 has the rider writing "coming down now" at 11:02:47; EV-GPS-03303's rider track instead holds the device stationary at 0.0 kph for every one of its 79 fixes, at a mean 698.8 m from the pickup pin (min 694.4 m, max 702.0 m) across the whole window from 10:57:30 to 11:09:13, with rider_qualifying_fix_count 0 against the 100 m presence radius. POL-NS-11 does not rescue the position either way, because the track is present rather than absent, and POL-NS-04 limb (c) cannot be run in the rider's favour on those fixes. The conflict is left standing, so the disputed $4.50 is held rather than collected or refunded while a reviewer settles what the rider's position actually was.

This is a repeat pair on the two counters limb (c) of POL-NS-09 reads: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d stands at 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d stands at 2, so those fields together show 2 or more disputes involving this rider and this driver in the trailing 90 days, and the limb routes the case to a human reviewer with no monetary ruling and the $4.50 held rather than collected or refunded. Escalation is terminal, and on this record it is the only disposition that does not simply leave the rider's money where it is while a repeated pattern between the same two accounts goes unexamined. The open question the reviewer must settle is whether those two counters concern disputes between this same rider and driver, which the profile snapshots do not break down.

The rider does not claim that POL-NS-04 exonerates on this export, and the judge should not have to find the gap unaided: limb (c) requires the rider's device inside the 100 m presence radius for the majority of qualifying fixes, and EV-GPS-03303's rider track places it 694 to 702 m from the pin with no qualifying fix inside that radius. That failed limb does not establish that the rider was absent as a fact - it leaves rider presence an unanswered question, which is precisely the question limb (b) of POL-NS-09 exists to hand to a reviewer. The rider's case on the fee rests on that review route, not on an exoneration the track does not support.

The money at stake is live and unrefunded, so the direction of any disposition matters. EV-FARE-03303 shows the cancellation_fee line at 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, against a contested amount of $4.50. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative and on this rider-filed dispute leaves exactly that state standing - the rider recovers nothing; the only outcomes that move this rider's money are a refund of that line or an escalation that holds it pending review.

Every limb of the baseline test holds on this record. (a) The trip record carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 11:00:27. (b) The GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from exactly that timestamp — dwell_start_offset_sec is 0.0, so limb (b) is satisfied at, not after, the marker. (c) He then held position inside the geofence for a continuous 410 seconds, more than twice the 180 second free waiting period in force for this trip, and no_show_threshold_sec is null so no longer threshold applies. (d) The trip carries no boarding event and was terminated by the driver at 11:07:18 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, 411 seconds after the dwell — which is at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed. All four limbs are carried, no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces them, and the cancellation fee is legitimately chargeable.

The arrival geofence test is satisfied on the driver's own fixes, not merely on his word. The trace contains 42 qualifying in-radius fixes running continuously from 11:00:27 to 11:07:17, comfortably past the three-consecutive-fix minimum. Note the zone class recorded in the trip record: this is a STANDARD pickup, so the correct radius is the tight 50 m — not the 120 m or 150 m that applies at large venues, hubs and the airport. The driver satisfies the strictest version of the test.

The waiting-period arithmetic runs in the driver's favour. Measured in-geofence dwell is 410 seconds against a 180 second minimum for STANDARD — a shortfall of -230 seconds, i.e. 230 seconds of surplus. There is no shortfall here for anyone to found a refund on, and the refund route in POL-NS-06 is simply not reached.

The arrival marker is genuine and no false-arrival finding lies against this driver. The first qualifying in-geofence fix falls at 11:00:27 — the very timestamp of the 'arrived' event, dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0 — and the trace shows him stationary (0.0 km/h appears among his distinct speeds) rather than travelling at the 15 km/h or above that would falsify the marker, and he was not more than 300 m from the pin. Even if the marker were impugned, POL-NS-05 limb (iii) preserves the fee: the corrected dwell of 410 seconds still meets the minimum in force, so the fee stands.

The rider's exoneration clause cannot run on her own evidence. POL-NS-04 limb (c) requires the rider's device to lie within the 100 m STANDARD presence radius for the majority of her qualifying fixes across the waiting window. Her track contains 79 fixes whose nearest approach to the pin is 694.4 m and whose mean is 698.8 m, with zero qualifying fixes inside the radius. Limb (c) is therefore affirmatively failed on admissible fixes, not undecidable, and POL-NS-04 does not apply.

POL-NS-03 is the wrong-entrance clause and it has no purchase on these facts. It applies where the driver's stationary fixes lie outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin. Here the stationary fixes lie inside the radius — that is precisely what makes them qualifying fixes under POL-NS-02 — so the 400 m ceiling and the wrong-entrance outcome are never reached, and no refund flows from this route.

The driver is owed his payout, and his own profile does not withhold it. POL-NS-07 fixes compensation at 80 percent of the $4.50 fee in force — $3.60 — and the anti-farming guard is run only on the two fields the clause names. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, far short of the 4 the count limb requires; and 1 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 86 is 0.012, far below the 0.08 rate limb. Both limbs of the guard must trip and neither does, so the compensation is paid rather than withheld, and the ruling follows POL-NS-07 as DRIVER_COMPENSATION at $3.60.

The trip record, the GPS trace and the chat log all carry COMPLETE admissibility at weight 1.0 with no issue codes — 100 percent trace coverage, a 10 second cadence, zero gaps, both tracks present, and sequence numbering intact in the chat. The facts that decide this case are therefore carried by undiscounted evidence, the POL-GEN-02(2) confidence cap is 1.0, and no finding needs to survive a discount.

The money is arithmetically sound and there is no integrity defect to complain of. The ledger's cancellation-fee line is $4.50, which is exactly the net figure in force under this trip's own platform_policy (cancellation_fee_sgd 4.50), and POL-NS-08(d) permits that line to show either the net figure or the rider's gross figure of $6.61. $4.50 is what the policy authorises and $4.50 is what was charged.

The rider's messages and her own track contradict the account in her claim. She wrote 'coming down now' at 11:02:47, but her device was stationary — 0.0 km/h at every recorded fix — and roughly 695 to 702 m from the pin from 10:57:30 through 11:09:13. She was not a few minutes late to a car at the pin; her device never came near it. The driver had already messaged her at 11:00:52 ('hi im at the pickup point, where are you') and waited a further four and a half minutes, until 11:07:18, before cancelling.

The rider's only counter under POL-NS-06 is the accumulation limb, and it is unavailable twice over. The trace shows a single in-geofence run, so there is no second interval for limb (i) to add to the first; and no traffic advisory exists for this pickup road at all — EV-ADVIS-03303-01 is MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0 — so there is nothing on file that could have made holding position lawfully impossible. I rely on the absence of that artifact, not on its content: the whole of the dwell is the one continuous 410 second run.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the $4.50 is not being refunded and the driver is not being paid by this automated ruling — the case is going to a human reviewer, and the fee stays on hold. Here is why.

The no-show is verified on the merits. The trip record (EV-TRIP-03303) shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 11:00:27 and the 180-second free waiting period started at 11:00:29; he cancelled at 11:07:18 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-03303) places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius continuously for 410 seconds from 11:00:27, on 42 qualifying fixes — a surplus of 230 seconds over the 180 seconds required — and no longer threshold applies (no_show_threshold_sec is null). All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold. There is no false-arrival point: the first in-geofence fix is at the arrival marker itself (offset 0.0 s) and he was stationary within the radius, so POL-NS-05 does not fire and no false-arrival referral is recorded.

The rider's refund routes do not open. POL-NS-04 fails at limb (c): the rider's device (EV-GPS-03303 rider track) sits 694–702 m from the pin on all 79 fixes, with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius, so the clause does not exonerate her — and POL-NS-11 does not apply, because the track is present rather than absent. Her 11:02:47 'coming down now' message does not contradict the trace on rider presence: it is a forward-looking coordinating statement, and the records agree she was not at the pin, so POL-NS-09(b) is not engaged. POL-NS-03 does not apply (the driver's stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius, not outside it within 400 m). POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to work on. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-03303-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; it carries no fact and is not needed here.

What sends this to a reviewer is a repeat-dispute signal. Both profiles record 2 disputes with the counterparty in the trailing 90 days (EV-RPROF-03303 and EV-DPROF-03303, both weight 1.0). POL-NS-09(c) reads those two fields together and escalates where they show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver; 2 meets that threshold. Escalation is terminal: no refund issues, no compensation issues, and the disputed $4.50 is held rather than collected or refunded.

For completeness: on the merits alone POL-NS-07 would have paid the driver 80% of the $4.50 fee in force, i.e. $3.60 (the figure the fare ledger itself carries), the anti-farming check not tripping — no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the count of 4, and 1/86 = 0.012, below the rate of 0.08. That $3.60 is part of what the reviewer decides. The fare ledger reconciles: the $4.50 charged equals the net fee in this trip's platform_policy, and POL-NS-08(d) also permits the $6.61 gross figure, so there is no fare-integrity defect. Every deciding artifact carries weight 1.0, so the confidence cap under POL-GEN-02(2) is 1.0 and confidence is set at 0.9 — not a trigger under POL-NS-09(a).

The reviewer should settle two open questions: (1) whether the two recorded counterparty disputes are in fact no-show disputes between this same rider and driver; and (2) whether, on the verified no-show, the driver's $3.60 payout should be released. The monetary effect at this stage is zero and the amount stays frozen.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
